subject_session: Achilles_10252013 (primary); all 8 sessions across 4 rats analyzed
stated_limitation: raw spatial information in bits per spike is not comparable across cells with different spike counts. In this data set the excitatory units that *fail* the place-cell test have a higher median raw spatial information (1.03 bits/spike) than the units that pass it (0.65 bits/spike), because sparse firing produces noisy, spiky rate maps that score well on any map-shape statistic

justification.dataset: DANDI:000044 (Grosmark & Buzsáki dorsal CA1) is the canonical known-good place-cell dataset, with the primary session a standard linear-track recording.
justification.handling: Real data streamed via remfile with disk cache, correct excitatory/inhibitory unit typing, explicit 5 cm/s speed threshold, lap segmentation validated in fig00, and per-cell spike-count criteria.
justification.analysis: Skaggs spatial information with a per-cell circular-shift null, directional rate maps, Bayesian decoding on held-out laps, odd/even stability, and a Poisson GLM controlling for the speed confound are all appropriate and correctly implemented.
justification.correctness: Every headline number (68% place cells, 0.677 bits/spike, 32 cm width, 7.3 Hz peak, 5.2 cm decode error) traces to the committed CSVs, is internally consistent with the figures, and rests on sound shuffle/held-out statistics across all 8 sessions.
justification.figures: Figures are clear, axes carry units and sample sizes, example cells are ordered by field position rather than cherry-picked by effect magnitude, and each claim (tiling, remapping, decoding, GLM) is directly visible.
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate to strong, clean evidence, and the write-up plainly names non-obvious caveats such as raw SI being non-comparable across spike counts and weak interneuron spatial modulation, showing genuine calibration rather than overstatement.
